full_judgment: 7. Successive criminal cases for commission of grave offences like murder, rape, riot, looting, arson or for repeated criminal offences of serious nature tending to incite interference with the administration of law or the maintenance of law and order may be grounds for preventive detention as envisaged under section 2(f)(v) of the Special Powers Act. In the instant case we do not find such materials before us. The respondents have not filed any affidavit in opposition. Rule 39 of the High Court Rules make it obligatory on the respondents to show because and if no cause is shown the rule is that the person or persons improperly detained shall be set at liberty. This rule may be interpreted to mean that to justify the detention of a detenu the detaining authority is under an obligation to file the affidavit-in-opposition to discharge its burden of proof that the detenu is not being held in custody without lawful authority or in an unlawful manner. But the rule is not inflexible and that in all cases under Article 102(2)(b )(i) an affidavit-in-opposition is mandatory on the part of the respondents. If it is manifest from the writ petition itself that the causes or manner of detention stands adequately explained and justified on the face of it, the respondents need not file an affidavit-in-opposition and may support the detention orally see 1995 BLD (AD) 248.
